source_title: Your favorite YouTube channel could suddenly appear blank — here’s why
source_excerpt:

YouTube is testing a new cleanup process that gives certain channels facing termination over spam violations a second chance.
Eligible creators have 30 days to fix or remove offending videos, or delete their entire video library to avoid termination.
Creators who wipe their videos can retain their subscribers, channel handle, and monetization status, potentially leaving viewers with empty channels in their subscriptions. Preview
Imagine heading to YouTube to revisit an old video from one of your favorite creators, only to find that the video, and in some cases, the creator’s entire library, has vanished. You’d normally blame YouTube, but soon, the platform might not be the culprit.
The streaming giant is testing a new approach to dealing with channels that violate certain spam policies, and it includes giving creators the chance to voluntarily delete videos to save their channel from being terminated .
For reference, traditionally, channels found guilty of repeated or serious spam policy violations faced the possibility of permanent termination. It was a complete execution, which meant losing everything associated with the channel, including all videos and the subscribers amassed over the years. The only recourse was submitting an appeal. Now, YouTube is offering a different recourse .
The company is experimenting with a new “cleanup” option for terminated channels. “Instead of immediate channel termination, eligible channels will now have the opportunity to self-correct, edit, or remove the violative content,” wrote YouTube.
A fresh start, without losing your subscribers
YouTube explained that if a channel is eligible for the experiment and is bound to be terminated, it will enter a 30-day locked period. During this time, they can’t upload new videos or post comments. They will, however, be able to leverage these new cleanup remedies to save their channel.
These are like being put in detention. The punishment is still there, but there’s an opportunity to make things right. The first option is to identify the videos that violate YouTube’s policies and either edit them or remove them entirely. This will be subject to YouTube’s review.
The second option is more drastic. Creators can delete all uploaded videos to immediately unlock their channel. The measure lets you start fresh while keeping your subscribers, channel handle, and even your YouTube Partner Program (YPP) status. The option to appeal YouTube’s decision remains. Failing to address the issue within 30 days will ultimately lead to termination.
So if you find a channel you’ve been subscribed to for years without any of its videos, it might not mean that the channel has been abandoned. Instead, the creator might have voluntarily wiped it to avoid losing the channel altogether.
